title: fix(plugins): keep Lossless usable after settings reload
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Lossless recall can fail with a closed database after a settings reload. OpenClaw registers the replacement before cleaning up its predecessor, so old cleanup can invalidate the replacement's resources.

## User Impact

Plugin settings reload without restarting the Gateway. OpenClaw drains and disposes the old registration before acquiring replacement resources. If replacement fails before publication and cleanup succeeds, it automatically registers captured previous code and settings with fresh resource ownership. Unchanged plugins retain their registrations.

Cleanup is a safety barrier: delayed cleanup can be retried after settlement; an actual cleanup failure leaves the affected plugin fenced instead of admitting another resource owner. Healthy sibling channels resume independently after failed command-owner cleanup. Recovery restores the runtime, without rewriting externally edited configuration files.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep validation, source capture, resource handoff, publication, and recovery in the existing reload owner. Captured-source recovery also works after installed files are replaced or removed. Package metadata hydration now preserves workspace provenance, descriptions, and normalized empty dependency maps so unchanged plugins are retained.

Integrated with [#149643](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149643), [#149644](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149644), [#149645](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149645), [#149646](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149646), and [#149648](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149648). The moved module loader, shared compiled-bundled code identity, fresh registration owners, and registry, inbound-registration, cached-error, and timer fixes are preserved.

## Evidence

**The combined packaged lifecycle matrix passed** on built commit `b7e9fe5e701c3cefc60c78cee95cd5f08a8d843a` (parent `d5ba4e3380a1fc061bb1eaf71a5ec33fed396073`): 79 CLI operations, 38 functional probes, 746 continuity samples, zero failed samples, 400.48 seconds. Official plugin runtime payloads and personal/work gateways are unmodified.

| Plugin | Install | Settings | Disable / enable | Uninstall / reinstall | Functional proof |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| IRC 2026.9.4 | Pass | Pass | Pass | Pass | Loopback PRIVMSG and persistent-client PONG |
| Voice Call 2026.9.4 | Pass | Pass | Pass | Pass | Mock call, webhook state change, end call; listener moved with its port setting |
| Lossless 1.0.0 | Pass | Pass | Pass | Pass | Recall, exact stored-row hash, failed replacement recovery |
| Diffs 2026.9.4 | Pass | Pass | Pass | Pass | Tool output, HTTP 200 viewer, dark-to-light setting |

- Gateway PID **49236** remained constant, with no internal-restart markers. Health stayed HTTP 200 at every sample. The synthetic sibling retained its exact instance with **1 registration / 1 start / 0 stops / 0 disposals**. Voice retained its exact listening socket across 450 samples and had no new listener-start events. No Canvas tool-inventory ownership errors or unhandled Gateway HTTP errors occurred.
- Invalid Lossless `databasePath` produced an ordered registration failure → fresh initialization on the original database → rejected activation. Recall and IRC worked **before repairing the rejected file setting**; the subsequent valid reload also passed. The one-row SHA256 remained `5371292ea6f39471a9bc99473e143ab18dc186aa1915ddeec98f3abec8948e26` through final reinstall. Official Lossless bundle SHA256 remained `865455165bc01cd37f3d3cf9f38eb025c2aa9eb1c702422a3625f526f3220c90`.
- IRC retained its persistent connection during unrelated Voice/Diffs operations. The existing command-refresh policy deliberately reconnects channels when Lossless `/lcm` ownership changes: all ten such operations completed exactly one bounded automatic reconnect and a functional probe before the next operation. Eighteen temporary CLI senders were individually verified and reconciled with all raw connection events. No channel-refresh policy changed.
- **1,137 tests passed across 38 files**, with one optional Bun skip; all changed-file gates passed. CI is green for the tested head. Paired regressions cover drain-timeout retries, cleanup barriers, fresh recovery, healthy sibling-channel resumption, pre-instance error retention, and unchanged metadata keeping registrations at `1→1→1` instead of `1→2→3`.

The unchanged published `openclaw@2026.9.4` updater also installed this exact candidate with its matching `@openclaw/ai` companion through the repository's loopback registry acceptance route: exit 0 in 66.94 seconds. All **11,215 core and 124 AI payload files** matched. Doctor passed 35 checks; Lossless recall and stored rows survived. Every prior config value was preserved, with only documented implicit-main roster and Doctor run metadata added. This application-upgrade cell uses separate baseline/candidate starts; same-PID proof applies to plugin operations above.

Before/after baseline: stack-only `d1dcf72bca77` changed recall HTTP 200→500 after a threshold reload at the same PID. The combined build above passes that operation and failed-replacement recovery. The later parent `be781c5356b245fce9a802f3fdb1d9686e6c79c6` only adds a Telegram test teardown drain; its runtime is unchanged.

Final integration: all five upstream PRs are now merged. Current head `cba099fa3da72b7e7e3b215fd86d9a3c6e3fd00c` replays all 14 fix commits patch-identically onto main `9976e84fa3a328983fd868426d5747a44266ef3a`. **837 focused integration tests passed in 10 files** on this head, covering reload/recovery, installed packages, startup/transcript capture, config, metadata, CLI policy, provider-policy generations, and cache/registry retention. The packaged evidence above remains attributed to the original tested build; [Exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35071078087) on the integrated head (143 successful checks, 42 skipped, one neutral report).

Limits: IRC uses a loopback server and Voice Call its mock provider. Cold Diffs loading can delay requests for roughly seven seconds; idle HTTP-client lifetime is not a plugin ownership guarantee. The final harness checks actual listener identity and real HTTP failures. Canvas coverage exercises tool-inventory ownership, not rendering or remote-node actions. This does not establish endurance performance or resolve baseline native-ESM owner retention. Earlier failed runs are retained; reader, sender, and listener corrections have independent negative controls.
